conviction_note: FY26 revenue, adjusted EBITDA and cash were all pre-released (17 Feb, 8 Oct, 9 Apr RNS), so the move lives in the first FY27 guide, a scheduled guidance event on a 49%-vol name. abs_move is therefore set near the 9% guidance base. p_up sits just under 50: firm order intake since the interims was thin (one 20 MW FID in the RNS record), which caps the FY27 revenue guide, and that roughly offsets a lower-loss FY26 base after the 8 Oct EBITDA upgrade. The findings sum (-1.1) and the scaled number (-0.68) agree in sign and are both small because neither direction rests on a number the market has not seen.

Year-end (30 Apr 2026) contracted backlog, against £152m 'to date' at the January interims. Likely flat to down, since about £22-25m of H2 revenue was burned and only the 20 MW MorGen POSEIDON converted to firm in the RNS record.

findings.finding: Since the January interims (backlog £152m 'to date'), the RNS record shows only one order converting to firm backlog: MorGen's 20 MW POSEIDON at FID (NtP 16 Feb, confirmed 11 Mar). Everything else is non-binding (DB Systemtechnik LOI, Protium partnership, Rheinmetall collaboration, Hydropulse 150 MW HoT; Stablegrid's 30 MW FID 'expected in 2026' and RWE's 150 MW call-offs are not announced). Meanwhile about £22-25m of H2 FY26 revenue was recognised, so the year-end backlog and the first FY27 revenue guide are constrained.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-guide days: FY26 guide at the Aug 2025 prelims (+50% revenue growth guided) +9.0%; Aug 2024 prelims -6.4%; Jan 2026 interims (guide reiterated, backlog £152m) -6.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -12.5% over 20 sessions. But that move tracks the sector (Plug -30.6%, Ceres -23.0% over the same 20 sessions, Yahoo tape), not an ITM order shortfall. Nobody publishes an ITM backlog roll-forward, and the size of the FY27 guide is not knowable until the release. If the shortfall were priced, the 8 Oct EBITDA upgrade would not have closed +2.7%, and the consensus FY27 revenue would have been cut on the record. The only snippet shows a cut from ~£71m to ~£58m between March and July, so it may be partly in.
findings.independence: Interims call (3 Feb 2026): CFO declined to predict book-to-bill; the backlog 'comprises only of fully contracted orders without any starting conditions' https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-itm-power-sees-record-revenue-in-h1-2026-93CH-4480839 ; secondary German press reports book-to-bill fell from 5.5 to about 4 (snippet only, unverified) https://trading-treff.de/trading/itm-power-aktie-42-prozent-crash-vor-juni-entscheidungen

findings.finding: The 8 Oct RNS cut the FY26 adjusted EBITDA loss to £20-21m, 27% better than guided and 38% better year on year, with revenue unchanged. That lowers the cost and legacy-loss base the FY27 EBITDA guide starts from: legacy contracts were 29% of backlog in January and due to roll off over about 18 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 8 Oct EBITDA upgrade itself closed +2.73% (89.60p to 92.05p) and the gain had faded to 90.00p by 15 Oct. The name sells its pre-released good news.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY26 number is priced (public 8 Oct). The transmission into FY27 EBITDA is not knowable until the guide, and the stock gave back the upgrade, which is what an unpriced read-through would look like. Only an inference, so sized small.
findings.independence: Interims RNS: 71% of the £152m backlog was profitable, up from 60%, with the legacy portion being worked through https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/itm-power--itm/half-year-financial-report/9392466

findings.finding: Hydropulse's 150 MW BOO Heads of Terms (12 Oct) commits ITM to a capital-heavy model ('constructive discussions with banks on project-level financing'). The first FY27 cash guide must carry FEED and Hydropulse build-out alongside the Chronos line capex. The money buys 10-year contracted recurring revenue, but FID is 2027, so most capex falls after FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 12 Oct HoT day closed +0.7% (93.85p to 94.55p) after intraday gains reported at 4-7%. The 9 Apr GB Energy equity plus grant (a cash-guide raise) started the run from ~63p to ~194p.
findings.why_not_priced: The cash cost of the BOO model has not been quantified anywhere. FY26 cash guidance (£210-215m) predates the HoT and excludes Hydropulse, so the first number arrives with the FY27 cash guide.
findings.independence: Interims call: CEO had 'not given a specific price' on Hydropulse capex and described modelling full CapEx and OpEx https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-itm-power-sees-record-revenue-in-h1-2026-93CH-4480839

findings.finding: The pre-print drawdown is sector-wide and the short is covering. ITM -12.5% over 20 sessions against Plug -30.6%, Ceres -23.0% and thyssenkrupp nucera -6.7% on the same tape. FCA aggregate short fell 2.42% to 2.22% by 14 Oct, and the large spring shorts (Helikon 2.63%, Qube 1.30%) were cut below disclosure by May.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The June 2026 sector rout (Goldman sell, Ballard -19%) took ITM down 27% in a week.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It agrees with the baseline's positive short-squeeze/covering lean, so it is sized near zero. Filed because the sector beta, not company news, explains the 20-day run-up the free control reads.

findings.finding: This is the first-year audit by new auditor BDO, under a newly adopted percentage-of-completion policy. Results came about 9 weeks later than FY25's (14 Aug 2025 vs 19 Oct 2026), and the Annual Report will miss the AGM. This leaves a small tail risk of audit-driven changes to the reported FY26 numbers or disclosures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior audit-related event at ITM in the RNS record read.
findings.why_not_priced: The delay is public, and the 8 Oct EBITDA upgrade three days later suggests the audited numbers were essentially settled. So this is near zero and only the tail is unpriced.

baseline_tension: Mild tension: the baseline lean is +2.36 (short-squeeze and covering components) and the 20-day run-up of -12.5% invites a mean-reversion long, while the one company-level finding with weight (thin firm intake caps the FY27 guide) leans negative. language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry: the domestic UK half (Investegate RNS archive, AJ Bell/Alliance News, the FCA per-holder file) supplied the primary documents. The PDMR-free run of order RNS since March came from reading the issuer's own RNS list rather than wire copy, but that list is English and international readers can reach it equally.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' plus 'a first guide for a new fiscal year is a scheduled guidance event' raised abs_move_pct from 7.0 to 8.5, toward the 9.0% guidance-change median, despite the pre-released FY26 lines.

'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' cut the audit/reported-line finding from -0.3 to -0.2 and the EBITDA-transmission finding from +0.6 to +0.5, since the FY26 EBITDA is public.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' moved the Hydropulse/FY27 cash finding from -0.3 to -0.4.
